questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A river originates in Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh), flows westward through a rift valley for approximately 1,312 km, and empties into the Arabian Sea through a broad estuary. Which river is this?
questions.explanation: Narmada (1,312 km) originates at Amarkantak (MP), flows WESTWARD through a rift valley between Vindhya and Satpura ranges, and enters the Arabian Sea via an estuary near Bharuch (Gujarat). It does NOT form a delta. Tapti also flows west but originates in Betul (MP) and is shorter (724 km).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Identify the correct north-to-south order of these hill stations:
questions.explanation: North to South along the Himalayas: Shimla (31.1°N, HP) → Mussoorie (30.4°N, Uttarakhand) → Nainital (29.4°N, Uttarakhand) → Darjeeling (27.0°N, West Bengal). Darjeeling is the southernmost as it's in the Eastern Himalayas. Shimla is the northernmost among these options.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A state in India shares borders with three countries (China, Nepal, Bhutan) and four Indian states. It is also home to the Kangchenjunga peak. Identify the state:
questions.explanation: Sikkim shares borders with China (Tibet - north), Nepal (west), Bhutan (east), and Indian states of West Bengal (south). Kangchenjunga (8,586m, 3rd highest in world) is on the Sikkim-Nepal border. Sikkim is India's least populous state and second smallest by area.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Consider a strait that is approximately 80 km wide at its narrowest point, separates India from Sri Lanka, and contains a chain of limestone shoals historically called Adam's Bridge. This strait is:
questions.explanation: Palk Strait (53-80 km wide) separates Tamil Nadu from northern Sri Lanka. Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu) is a chain of limestone shoals connecting Pamban Island (India) to Mannar Island (Sri Lanka). Ten Degree Channel separates Andaman from Nicobar. Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from Maldives. Duncan Passage separates South Andaman from Little Andaman.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A river system in India has its origin in Tibet (where it is called Tsangpo), enters India through Arunachal Pradesh (where it is called Dihang/Siang), and flows through Assam creating the world's largest river island (Majuli). Identify the river:
questions.explanation: Brahmaputra: Tsangpo (Tibet) → Dihang/Siang (Arunachal) → Brahmaputra (Assam) → Jamuna (Bangladesh). It creates Majuli (world's largest river island, Assam). It's an antecedent river (older than Himalayas). Male river name (Brahma+putra = son of Brahma). Highly braided in Assam, causing frequent floods.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Identify the INCORRECT pair of ports and their coastal location:
1. Kandla - Gulf of Kutch (West coast)
2. Paradip - Odisha coast (East coast)
3. Tuticorin - Kerala coast (West coast)
4. Visakhapatnam - Andhra Pradesh coast (East coast)
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is INCORRECT. Tuticorin (Thoothukudi) is in TAMIL NADU on the EAST coast (Gulf of Mannar side), NOT Kerala west coast. Kandla (Gujarat, west coast, tidal port), Paradip (Odisha, east coast, iron ore export), Visakhapatnam (AP, east coast, deepest landlocked harbour) are all correctly matched.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A volcanic island in the Andaman Sea is the only active volcano in South Asia. It last erupted in 2020. Identify it:
questions.explanation: Barren Island (Andaman & Nicobar, India) is South Asia's only confirmed active volcano. Located 135 km NE of Port Blair. It has erupted multiple times: 1991, 1994-95, 2005-06, 2017, 2020. Narcondam is a dormant volcano. Car Nicobar is a coral island. Ross Island is a historic British administrative centre.

mapData.location: Andaman Sea, 135km NE of Port Blair

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Eastern and Western Ghats meet at which location?
questions.explanation: The Eastern and Western Ghats converge at the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu/Karnataka/Kerala junction). Anai Mudi (2,695m, in Cardamom Hills, Kerala) is the highest peak in SOUTH India but is not where the Ghats meet. Dodda Betta (2,637m) is the highest peak in the Nilgiris where the two Ghats converge.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following groups of islands are of CORAL origin?
1. Lakshadweep
2. Andaman Islands
3. Nicobar Islands
4. New Moore Island (now submerged)
questions.explanation: Only Lakshadweep and New Moore Island are/were coral origin. Andaman and Nicobar Islands are of VOLCANIC/tectonic origin (part of a submerged mountain chain extending from Myanmar's Arakan Yoma). Lakshadweep (36 islands) are coral atolls built on submarine ridge. New Moore/South Talpatti (disputed India-Bangladesh) was a sandy coral island that submerged due to sea level rise.
